summary:
Well, the dustjacket for FLOW MY TEARS is in my opinion the very best I’ve ever had on any book of mine and I am just so excited that words fail me (words never really fail me, but if they ever did they would now). And from your standpoint it’s a damn fine professional cover and should increase sales, inas­ much as I doubt if any other jackets in the stalls these days will draw the buyer’s eye more swiftly; it has drama to it, and intensity and so forth, and (here is what also astonished me) I had never ever been absolutely positive that the tide was a topnotch one, but the tide looks WONDERFUL on the jacket—it just reaches out along with the rest of the cover and, as they say, grabs you. 

Then I noticed you had after all gone ahead with a photo of me on the back cover instead of the quote from the book, and that made me happy, too—not so much because I always wondered what I looked like or something but because the original excerpt from the novel which you had planned for the back cover would have handed the reader in advance the crucial passage before he even started reading it, which would have vitiated my point in writing it So in two ways, I’m pleased you dropped the excerpt and put on the photo. That photo, by the way, was taken while I was autographing books at a bookstore, shot by a little chicano girl so shy that she would never tell me her name—just call me “C.C.” she said. It was her idea, when she had developed all the shots she took and enlarged and cropped them...
